
=================================================================
#66 Nine Omens  (659)
Arc: The Fall of Euija · place: sabi · tone: omen dread
Logline: Every omen is real, in the sense that people saw it. That was always the only sense that mattered.
=================================================================
[0] ¶ Every one of the nine signs is real, in the sense that people saw it. That was always the only sense that mattered, and the man who taught Baekje so is about to find out how much he meant it.
[1] ¶ Foxes walk into the Assembly hall in a pack, and a white one sits down on the Premier’s desk. A hen mates with a sparrow. A dead fish as long as a boat washes up on the river. Then a dead woman, longer than the fish.
[2] ¶ The palace trees weep at night. The White River turns red with blood. Toads gather in the tops of the trees by the ten thousand. Storm winds, rain, lightning, and black clouds fighting like dragons over the temples. Last, a ghost runs into the palace shouting, and burrows into the ground. They dig, and find a turtle.
[3] ¶ They bring the turtle to the king in a lacquer box. He turns it over in his hands like a forgery he is pricing.
[4] King Euija: Three feet down, under my own palace. / Who buried you, little one? / …Hm. Somebody with good taste in shells.
[5] ▼ FLASHBACK 659 A room in Surabol, some months earlier
    [5.0] King Muyeol: For twenty years Euija has been selling his people miracles. / Dragons. White deer.
    [5.1] Kim Yushin: Knowing they were false?
    [5.2] King Muyeol: He made them himself. / Which makes him the worst reader of signs alive. / He has spent his whole life knowing that signs are made by hands.
    [5.3] Kim Yushin: …Then why would it work on him?
    [5.4] King Muyeol: It doesn’t have to work on him. / It only has to work on his people.
    [5.5] ¶ He does not order any of it, exactly. He asks for men who can travel, he asks what the markets of Sabi are frightened of, and he asks how deep one has to bury a turtle shell for the finding of it to look like an accident.
    [5.6] King Muyeol: An army is the last thing you need to bring down a country. / First you need a rumour. / And you build a rumour out of what the people are already afraid of.
[5] ▲ end flashback
[6] Baekje: Baekje falls! Baekje falls!
[7] ── SCENE: The Shaman ──
[8] ¶ He keeps a shaman on retainer the way other kings keep song-girls. He likes watching someone else believe the sky talks; he has told Gyebek the gods are cheap civil servants, and told Gesomun the same with wine on his breath. The shaman thinks he is frightened. He lets her.
[9] King Euija: I came for amusement today. / There are nine. / Read them.
[10] The Shaman: The foxes — the politicians are corrupt. / The hen and the sparrow — public morals have declined. / The great fish — the economy is in decline. / The great woman’s corpse — the people suffer for it.
[11] The Shaman: The ghost-screams — the forgotten common man cries out. / The blood-red river — the public sphere is polluted. / The toads in the trees — only lying peddlers have loud voices. / The dragon-clouds — the nation begins fighting itself.
[12] King Euija: …The turtle. / From the shell.
[13] ❝QUOTE (Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 28, Baekje Annals — King Uija, yr. 20 (660); Lee Byong-do ed., vol. 1, p. 386): They obtained a tortoise; on its back was writing that said: Baekje is like the full moon; Silla is like the new moon.❞
[14] The Shaman: To be like a full moon is to be full — and what is full must wane — / to be like a crescent is to be not yet full — and what is not yet full grows fuller. / Baekje wanes. Silla fills.
[15] King Euija: You wretch!!!
[16] ¶ The blade is out before the last word cools. He cuts her down where she sits. The turtle’s sentence stays in the room.
[17] ¶ People start saying it out loud in the markets, which is how you know it is already over.
[18] Satek Chunbok: Your Majesty. What you need right now is not wine.
[19] Satek Chunbok: Your Majesty… / Say one name. / I will go and bring him.
[20] King Euija: …That name was one I made up. / When I was a prince on a mudbank.
[21] Satek Chunbok: …Your Majesty.
[22] King Euija: What are they saying in the markets these days.
[23] Satek Chunbok: …That Baekje is the full moon.
[24] King Euija: …Yes. / Well made.
[25] ¶ He never says that the signs were made. He could name the price of every piece of it. To say _a man made this one_ is to say it about the dragon over the Sabi, and the white deer, and the twenty years in between.
[26] ¶ The best lie a man ever tells is the one he cannot afford to expose.
[27] ── SCENE: The White River ──
[28] ¶ That night he leaves the palace the way he left it as a boy — without asking, without banners. The White River is waiting where it always waited. The omen said it ran red. Under the moon it is only black water and the smell of wet stone.
[29] ¶ He has spent years drowning on dry land: wine, women, and a letter he never sent to the man he never sent for. The river does not care. It knew him before the crown.
[30] King Euija: I named you here. / I will not die drunk on the bank of my own invention.
[31] ¶ He jumps. The cold takes the wine off him. When he surfaces he is coughing, furious, awake — the promising prince the eight clans once feared, scraped clean by the same river that taught him friendship.
[32] King Euija: Summon Gyebek…!
[33] ¶ Chunbok has followed him down with a lamp, the way a careful man follows a king who might be about to do something historic. He holds out a dry robe. The king does not take it.
[34] Satek Chunbok: Majesty, you’ll catch your death— / As Your Majesty well knows, a boat to Tamla takes time. / And the markets… forgive me. The markets are asking whether there will be a Baekje for him to come home to.
[35] King Euija: Let them ask. / We were a younger son’s house from the very start, Chunbok. Goguryeo got the hall. We got the road south. / Seven hundred years on a borrowed road, and we’re still here.
[36] Satek Chunbok: …For now, Majesty.
[37] King Euija: ‘For now.’ Ha. / That’s exactly what they told the first one, too.
[38] ¶ **Will Baekje survive? To answer that, go back to how it began: a mother, two sons, and a father who already had one…!**
